answer: An adversary who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the violet history. Churn is counted in zenith, and ripple publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 17% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 417 account operation therefore ties up 5 million dollars of idle capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
